metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., +0.70 or 0.00), suggesting overshoot bias.
- When sentiment turns negative (e.g., -0.30 or lower) in the last 3–5 days, model tends to hold high forecasts; should reduce forecast by 2–5% to align with mean reversion.
- Forecasts lag behind true outcomes by 1–3 days in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp price drops; adjust for 1-day lag correction.
- If sentiment is positive and price is rising, model often fails to anticipate sharp reversals; apply a 1–2 day “cool-down” buffer before expecting peak.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (e.g., alternating +0.70 and -0.30), model overfits recent trends; use 3-day moving average smoothing to reduce noise.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows a sharp drop after a peak, model often fails to recognize it; apply a “reversal penalty” of 3–5% below peak for 2–5 days post-peak.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over last 5 days, model should not forecast above 10% above recent 7-day average; cap forecast at 10% below recent high.
